name: Sheryl Sandberg
role: Former Meta chief operating officer and founder of LeanIn.Org
summary: Sandberg argues that workplace and family arrangements systematically hold women back and calls for women to share leadership and spouses to share authority at home. She advocates national paid family leave and has funded efforts to protect legal access to abortion.

state-harmful.rationale: Sandberg and Thomas urged Congress to enact a nationwide social insurance program funded through payroll taxes.

traditional-family.rationale: In Breathing Again in Option B, Sandberg and Grant call for society to embrace families regardless of form and extend support to single parents, unmarried partners, and same-sex couples.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Sandberg served as honorary co-chair of Silicon Valley Leaders Say NO on Proposition 8, which publicly campaigned to preserve same-sex couples’ right to marry in California.

abortion-legal.rationale: Sandberg committed $3 million to the ACLU’s nationwide effort to oppose abortion bans in legislatures and protect abortion access through ballot measures after Roe was overturned.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: In her 2020 statement Sandberg argued that addressing racial injustice required active steps and backed Juneteenth fundraising for racial-justice organizations and targeted investment in Black communities.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: In response to Senator Lankford, Sandberg defended encryption as necessary to keep private messages secure and affirmed her commitment to continuing to offer it on WhatsApp, which she understood to use end-to-end encryption.

taxation-theft.rationale: Sandberg and Thomas endorsed using a payroll tax to fund national paid family and medical leave, describing this as a responsible way to pay for the program.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: In her Call Me Back interview Sandberg stood by Israel and explicitly supported a peace settlement with two states.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: In Make Your Partner a Real Partner in Lean In, Sandberg criticizes laws that reinforce distinct roles through unequal leave eligibility and calls for men to participate fully in caregiving. Her national paid-leave proposal extends eligibility to workers of either sex.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The introduction to Lean In describes systemic workplace barriers for women, including bias in promotion, unequal access to mentors, and the career costs of having fewer options for combining employment and caregiving.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Sandberg and Thomas urged Congress to establish and fund a national paid family and medical leave program.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Sandberg signed an appeal to world leaders to provide the funds needed to bring education to the 130 million girls out of school around the world, highlighting the need in the poorest countries.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Sandberg co-chaired the business leaders’ campaign to preserve same-sex couples’ right to marry under California law.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: In A Letter to Graduates in Lean In for Graduates, Sandberg calls for recognizing and changing the biases that compound workplace barriers for women of color. In Breathing Again in Option B, she and Grant call for closing a wage gap that falls especially heavily on Black and Latina women.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: In Make Your Partner a Real Partner in Lean In, Sandberg describes equal say over household decisions as part of the marital partnership she advocates.

women-suffrage.rationale: In the introduction to Lean In, Sandberg explicitly embraces the suffragists’ goal of full equality and calls for women to exercise political leadership on the same terms as men.

work-centre-of-life.rationale: In the Lean In introduction Sandberg rejects a single template for success and presents a life centered on caring for others as an equally valuable choice.

women-organise-apart-from-men.rationale: In Working Together Toward Equality in Lean In, Sandberg calls for women and men to work together to change the stereotypes and institutional barriers that hold women back.

state-laws-apply-online.rationale: In her Senate testimony Sandberg supported the Honest Ads Act, which would extend legal disclosure rules for political advertising to online platforms.

notes: Reviewed Lean In, Option B, the added author letter in Lean In for Graduates, congressional testimony, interview transcripts, signed advocacy, and philanthropic records. Searched economic and labor policy, elections and courts, religion and civil liberties, racial and gender equality, migration and foreign aid, Israel and Palestine, military alliances and intervention, climate and energy, privacy and online regulation, and methods of social change. Her calls to preserve DACA and increase the federal minimum wage address specific programs or changes without specifying an overall immigration level or a statutory living-wage standard. Her Senate testimony addresses platform safety and ad transparency, and leaves most questions about institutions and civil liberties unanswered.
